newsitem.title: UK: UK's PIA promotes debate on personal investments.
newsitem.headline: UK's PIA promotes debate on personal investments.

text.p: The UK's Personal Investment Authority (PIA) on Thursday launched a discussion paper aimed at refining, simplifying and enhancing investor protection.
The PIA, which regulates firms involved in selling investments to private investors, said its proposals addressed the concerns of both the industry and consumer groups.
Issues include the information firms must give to investors and why the sales process can take a long time.

The PIA said the paper would discuss how the information given to investors "can be made more concise, simpler and more useful, so that individuals are better informed before they decide to buy investment products".

It said some investors found the process of buying "unduly intrusive and off-putting" and think firms are incurring unnecessary costs. As a result it was publishing detailed guidance to help streamline the process.
